summary: Tilak Kariyawasam is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as head of the Department of Pali and Buddhist Studies at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1993) and Dean of the Graduate School at International Buddhist College (attested 2014).

Tilmann Vetter (1937–2012) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Vienna (~1958–1962), studying under Erich Heintel and Erich Frauwallner, and became a professor at Leiden University in 1974.

Timothy Dubber is an Indology and history/archaeology researcher. Educated at the University of New South Wales Canberra and the University of Edinburgh, he became a PhD candidate at the Australian National University in 2025 and an Adjunct Fellow at UNSW in 2026.

Timothy Hugh Barrett is a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at the University of Cambridge and Yale University, he taught at Cambridge (attested 1981) before becoming a professor at SOAS University of London in 1986.

Timothy Lenz works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied as a graduate student at the University of Washington under Richard G. Salomon and Collett Cox (attested 1999) and later served there as professor (attested 2017) and faculty member (attested 2026).

Timothy Lubin is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Columbia and Harvard. He lectured at Harvard (1994–1996) and the University of Virginia (1996–1997) before becoming a professor at Washington and Lee University in 1997.
Tina Rasmussen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under traditional teacher Pa-Auk Sayadaw and completed an MA supervised by Christian K. Wedemeyer.

Tinatin Aleksandrovna Chavchavadze (1928–1997) studied at Tbilisi State University (~1944–1949). Her career in Iranian, Central Asian, Indological, and linguistic studies included posts at Tbilisi State University, the Institute of Linguistics, and the Giorgi Tsereteli Institute of Oriental Studies.

Tine Van Overberghe works in Indology and religious studies. She earned a bachelor's degree at Ghent University (2015–2020) and became an assistante diplômée (2022) and PhD student (2023) at the University of Lausanne.

Tine Vekemans is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She completed an MA at Ghent University (2003–2007) and holds the Ācārya Mahāprajña Chair for Jain Studies at Ghent University (attested 2026).

Tirtha Halder is an Indology and philosophy scholar. After studies at Gour Banga, Jadavpur, Baba Saheb Ambedkar Education, and Visva-Bharati universities, he began pursuing a PhD in Sanskrit at Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2022.

Tirumalai Krishnamacharya (1888–1989) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Mysore, Queen's College, and under Ramamohana Brahmachari. He taught at Maharaja's Sanskrit College, Mysore (1931) and Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College (~1952–1970).

Tissa Rajapatirana (1933–2021) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong (1966–1974) and held a post there in the Department of South Asian and Buddhist Studies (attested 1988).

Tista Biswas works in Indology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Subuddhi Charan Goswami and holds the Sir William Jones Research Fellowship in Sanskritic Studies at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Tiziana Pontillo is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She completed her PhD at the University of Milan (1996–2000), studied at the University of Cagliari in 2016, and became a full professor of Sanskrit language and literature at Cagliari in 2022.
Todar Mall was an Indology scholar who studied under Hermann Jacobi and Arthur Anthony Macdonell.
Todd A. Gibson is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under György Kara and earned his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington (attested 1991).

Todd Thornton Lewis studied at Columbia University under faculty including Alex Wayman and Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah. A religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology scholar, he held the Murray Distinguished Professorship and professorship of world religions at College of the Holy Cross (attested 2016–2017).

Tokan Tada (1890–1967) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sera Monastery (1913–1923). He held appointments at the University of Tokyo (1924), Tohoku University (1925), and Toyo Bunko's Tibetan Studies Research Center (1956).
Toke Lindegaard Knudsen is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied under Kim Plofker and completed his doctoral studies under David Pingree in 2008.
